summary: Liverpool Bay light on Western Head: a fog-signal station from the 1920s, a concrete tower from 1962, keepers to 1988, automated since; grounds open, tower closed.

structures.note: White octagonal tower with red top (Coast Guard). Heights disagree: NSLPS gives 50 ft (about 15.2 m); Lighthouse Friends gives 19.5 m.

visit.note: On foggy days the foghorn is very loud; the Region of Queens suggests hearing protection on the approach.

events.note: Lighthouse Friends: fog alarm placed in operation 1 October 1924 by Avery Covey, after a contract for the fog building, dwelling and oil store. NSLPS dates the fog alarm building to 1928; the Region of Queens dates the station to 1930. Disputed.
Radiobeacon established at Western Head; radio room built in place of an ell at the back of the fog alarm building.
Coffin Island keeper's dwelling in serious disrepair; the Region of Queens says Coffin Island was destaffed and a tower added to the Western Head fog alarm station.
Destaffed 1988 (Region of Queens); NSLPS: automated by 1988.

corrections.why: 1924 is the date the fog alarm went into operation, not the lighthouse. Lighthouse Friends says the lighthouse was not built until 1962, and NSLPS gives Year Lit 1962. The record's 1924 comes from Rowlett's 'Station established' note, which describes the fog station. The 1924 start itself is disputed (NSLPS 1928, Region of Queens 1930).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1924 first light and 1962 tower are both consistent once the fog station is separated from the tower. Lighthouse Friends says a foghorn has stood on the point since 1924 but the lighthouse was not built until 1962; NSLPS says the station was originally established as a foghorn station only.

notes_for_editor: (1) Fog-alarm start is disputed: 1 Oct 1924 (Lighthouse Friends), 1928 (NSLPS photo caption), 1930 (Region of Queens; NSLPS history items 'fog diaphone in operation' 1930). We searched the Department of Marine corpus for Western Head in all 25 volumes and found nothing; its reports end with fiscal 1923-24, so the 1924 fog contract and any 1928 or 1930 work are unverified by primary sources. (2) The first operator is Avery Covey (Lighthouse Friends, 1924) or Avery Curry (NSLPS, 1928). Lighthouse Friends also lists F.J. Curry for 1928 to 1930. Not linked. (3) Tower heights disagree: CCG 13.8 m; NSLPS 50 ft (about 15.2 m); Lighthouse Friends 19.5 m. We used CCG. (4) NSLPS gives the light's characteristic as Flashing White (1992); the CCG list gives Fl W 15s and we used it. (5) The record's first_lit 1924 is proposed for correction to 1962 (corrections). (6) Lawrence Wentzel is spelled Wentzell by NSLPS. (7) Moreau's start year is not given anywhere we read. (8) Lighthouse Friends draws on a book by Chris Mills, which we did not read; we used only Lighthouse Friends' statements. (9) The Wikipedia article for Western Head Lighthouse returned 404 and was not used. Genealogy pages turned up in search for the Hatt family; they were not used, and the family details here come from NSLPS's published account only. (10) No wreck or rescue was found. The wrecks list is empty and the story has no storm chapter. (11) The 1961 Coffin Island change is from the Region of Queens only. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28: (a) Story no longer says the fog station was 'not confirmed by a Department of Marine report' (a research-process claim, removed). (b) The fog-building remains and equipment are now given as Lighthouse Friends' 'today' description, not 'by 1988'. (c) Heights, Queens County and CCG ownership now have their own quotes (19.5 m LF; 50 ft NSLPS; County: Queens NSLPS; owned by CCG LF). (d) Metric-first units applied to the 15.2 m (50 ft) height. (e) The statement that the station 'grew out of a foghorn' is replaced by NSLPS's own wording that it was originally a foghorn station only.
